options.feedback: "Prefer" means you like one thing more than another; here you are saying you simply do not like onions.
"I think they are bad" matches the negative form "don't like", so that completes the answer.
"Love" means you like something very much, which is the opposite of "they are bad".
"Like" is the positive form; it does not match "I think they are bad".

questions.statement: Do you like pizza? - Yes, I ________.
questions.context: Learning about likes and dislikes (food) in English class.

options.feedback: In a short answer after "Do you...", the negative form is "don't", so it cannot be "Yes, I don't".
"Am" is the verb "be" used with "I"; the question "Do you like...?" needs "do" or "don't".
After "Yes, I", you repeat the auxiliary verb of the question, and the question is "Do you...?", so it is "do".
"Does" is used with he, she and it, not with "I".

questions.explanation:
This question evaluates apply skills regarding likes and dislikes (food) at the CEFR A1 level.

questions.statement: Do you like milk? - No, I ________.
questions.context: Learning about likes and dislikes (food) in English class.

options.feedback: "Yes, I do" answers "yes"; the short answer here starts with "No", so it cannot be "do".
"Doesn't" goes with he, she or it; the subject of this short answer is "I".
"Not" cannot stand alone as a short answer; it needs the auxiliary, as in "I don't".
After "No, I" you need the negative auxiliary "don't", so that completes the answer.

options.feedback: "My favorite food" is singular (one food), so it takes "is" in the present simple.
"Am" goes with the pronoun "I", not with a thing like "my favorite food".
"Are" is used with a plural subject; "food" here is singular.
"Be" is the plain form used after modals; a singular subject needs "is".

"Hate" means you dislike something a lot, which contradicts "it is my favorite".

"Has" is the verb for possession; the sentence is about liking, not owning.
